activity_context.topic_title: Triple Integrals Over Type II Regions

examples.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
\displaystyle \iint\limits_D \left[ \int_{0}^{z} \dfrac{\cos (2y)}{1-y} \,\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}A
$$

where the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane is given by

$$
D = \left\{ (y,z) \, : \, 0 \leq y \leq \dfrac{\pi}{6}, \: 0 \leq z \leq 2\sqrt{1-y} \right\}.
$$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{z}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}[x]_{x=0}^{x=z}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}(z-0)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{z\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the double integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{z\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}{\int }_{0}^{2\sqrt{1-y}}\frac{z\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}{[\frac{{z}^{2}}{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=2\sqrt{1-y}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)}{1-y}(\frac{4(1-y)}{2}-0)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =[\operatorname{sin}⁡(2y)]_{y=0}^{y=\pi /6} \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the type II region $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,yz\le x\le 4},
$$

where $D$ is some finite region in the $yz$-plane. Then,

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V=
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
A type II region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(y,z)\le x\le {u}_{2}(y,z)}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type II region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/1b49704bf6d5837a18d8b5dbb8b420d430d5e3881507540fb62a45cf1f6ce52f.png)

 

If $R$ is a type II region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(y,z)=yz\,{u}_{2}(y,z)=4.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{yz}^{4}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dA.
$$
